checks.question: Are important security, business, payment, job, migration, and integration events missing structured logs (missing structured logs for key events)? (OPS-001)

onYes.title: Fix missing structured logs (OPS-001): log key events with structured fields
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Without structured logs for key events, incidents are hard to investigate and audit.

Find all instances: Search important security/business/payment/job/migration/integration events for missing or unstructured logging.

Fix correctly: Emit structured logs with consistent event names and fields at the right level.

Constraints: Never log secrets/PII (CSP-002/CSP-017). Use the project's logging framework.

Acceptance: Key events are logged structurally. Add a test asserting the event log is emitted with expected fields.

checks.question: Are errors logged as info/debug, expected events logged as errors, or are logs noisy enough to obscure real failures (wrong log level/noisy logging)? (OPS-002)

onYes.title: Fix log levels (OPS-002): tune severity to actionability
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Wrong log levels hide real failures or flood logs with noise.

Find all instances: Search for errors logged below error level, normal events logged as errors, and noisy logs.

Fix correctly: Set log levels to match severity and operator actionability; reduce noise.

Constraints: Keep diagnostics useful. Coordinate with hot-path logging (PER-019).

Acceptance: Log levels reflect severity. Review/adjust the affected logs; add a check where feasible.

checks.question: Are request/job/message/trace identifiers not propagated across service boundaries (missing correlation/request ID propagation)? (OPS-003)

onYes.title: Fix correlation ID propagation (OPS-003): propagate IDs across boundaries
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Without correlation IDs, tracing a request across services/async work is nearly impossible.

Find all instances: Search service/async boundaries for missing propagation of request/correlation/trace IDs.

Fix correctly: Propagate correlation IDs through logs, metrics, traces, outbound headers, and async work; generate one at the edge if absent.

Constraints: Don't use high-cardinality IDs as metric labels (OPS-017).

Acceptance: Correlation IDs flow end to end. Add a test asserting the ID propagates across a boundary/async hop.

checks.question: Are key operations missing latency, throughput, error, saturation, or business-outcome metrics (missing critical-path metrics)? (OPS-004)

onYes.title: Fix missing metrics (OPS-004): add critical-path metrics
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Without metrics on critical paths, you can't detect or diagnose degradation.

Find all instances: Search user-visible and dependency-critical operations for missing latency/throughput/error/saturation/business metrics.

Fix correctly: Add metrics for these paths using the project's metrics system.

Constraints: Use bounded labels (OPS-017); no sensitive values in telemetry (OPS-018).

Acceptance: Critical paths are instrumented. Add a test/check asserting the metric is recorded.

checks.question: Are severe failures visible only in logs or user reports, not in metrics/alerts (no alertable failure signal)? (OPS-005)

onYes.title: Fix no alertable signal (OPS-005): expose alertable symptoms
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Failures only visible in logs go unnoticed until users complain.

Find all instances: Search severe failure paths for an alertable metric/signal.

Fix correctly: Expose SLO/error-budget or symptom-based alert signals (metrics) for severe failures.

Constraints: Alert on symptoms users feel, not just internals. Bounded labels (OPS-017).

Acceptance: Severe failures emit alertable signals. Add a test/check asserting the failure increments an alertable metric.

checks.question: Are there health checks that always return healthy or check irrelevant dependencies (weak health check)? (OPS-006)

onYes.title: Fix weak health check (OPS-006): check only relevant dependencies
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Health checks that always pass (or check the wrong things) mask outages and mislead orchestration.

Find all instances: Search health checks for always-healthy responses or checks of irrelevant dependencies.

Fix correctly: Check only the dependencies required for the health level being reported; reflect real health.

Constraints: Separate liveness from readiness (OPS-007). Don't leak internals (API-016).

Acceptance: Health checks reflect real dependency health. Add a test asserting the check fails when a required dependency is down.

checks.question: Is one health endpoint used both to restart the process and to decide traffic readiness (readiness/liveness mixed)? (OPS-007)

onYes.title: Fix mixed liveness/readiness (OPS-007): separate the two
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Conflating liveness and readiness causes needless restarts or routing of traffic to unready instances.

Find all instances: Search for a single health endpoint used for both restart and traffic decisions.

Fix correctly: Separate liveness (is the process alive) from readiness (can it serve traffic) with distinct checks.

Constraints: Liveness should not fail on transient dependency issues.

Acceptance: Liveness and readiness are distinct. Add tests asserting each reflects the correct condition.

checks.question: Are there defaults that enable debug mode, broad permissions, insecure transport, verbose errors, or weak limits in production (unsafe production default)? (OPS-008)

onYes.title: Fix unsafe production default (OPS-008): make defaults safe and fail closed
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Insecure defaults (debug on, verbose errors, broad permissions) expose production systems.

Find all instances: Search defaults for debug mode, broad permissions, insecure transport, verbose errors, and weak limits applied in production.

Fix correctly: Make production-safe defaults explicit and fail closed; require opt-in for risky settings.

Constraints: Config over hardcoding. Don't leak internals in errors (ERR-014).

Acceptance: Production defaults are safe. Add a test/check asserting risky features are off by default.

checks.question: Are mandatory config values replaced with implicit defaults when missing (required config silently defaulted)? (OPS-009)

onYes.title: Fix silently defaulted config (OPS-009): validate and fail fast
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Silently defaulting required config can run the system misconfigured or insecure.

Find all instances: Search config loading for required values that fall back to defaults.

Fix correctly: Validate required config at startup and fail fast with a clear message when absent/invalid.

Constraints: Distinguish required from optional. Config over hardcoding (ARC-011).

Acceptance: Missing required config aborts startup clearly. Add a test asserting startup fails when a required value is missing.

checks.question: Is configuration read during import/static initialization before environment and secrets are ready (config read too early)? (OPS-010)

onYes.title: Fix config read too early (OPS-010): load at controlled startup boundary
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Reading config at import/static-init time captures stale/empty values before env/secrets are ready.

Find all instances: Search for config/secret reads in static initializers or module top-level code.

Fix correctly: Load and validate runtime config at a controlled startup boundary, not at import/static init.

Constraints: Coordinate with config validation (OPS-009).

Acceptance: Config is read at a controlled boundary. Add a test/check confirming no static-init config reads remain.

checks.question: Are there feature flags without owner, removal criteria, expiry, or cleanup plan (feature flag lacks owner/expiry)? (OPS-011)

onYes.title: Fix unmanaged feature flags (OPS-011): add owner, expiry, and cleanup
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Long-lived orphan flags accumulate complexity and risk.

Find all instances: Search feature flags for missing owner, expiry, removal criteria, or cleanup plan.

Fix correctly: Record owner, expiry, and removal criteria; file/track a cleanup task; gate removal.

Constraints: Keep flag evaluation consistent (OPS-012).

Acceptance: Flags have owner/expiry/cleanup. Document or annotate the affected flags accordingly.

checks.question: Are feature-flag checks duplicated or applied inconsistently across UI, API, jobs, and permissions (feature flag inconsistently applied)? (OPS-012)

onYes.title: Fix inconsistent feature flags (OPS-012): centralize flag evaluation
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Inconsistent flag checks cause partial rollouts that expose half-enabled behavior.

Find all instances: Search for the same flag evaluated differently/duplicated across UI/API/jobs/permissions.

Fix correctly: Centralize flag evaluation and enforce consistent behavior across all layers.

Constraints: Keep flag semantics consistent. Coordinate with authorization (IAM-020).

Acceptance: Flags are evaluated consistently. Add a test asserting all layers honor the same flag state.

checks.question: Do schema/data migrations lack rollback, forward-fix, verification, or failure recovery (migration lacks rollback/forward-fix path)? (OPS-013)

onYes.title: Fix migration without recovery (OPS-013): add rollback/forward-fix
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Migrations without a recovery path can leave the database broken with no safe way back.

Find all instances: Search migrations for missing rollback/forward-fix, verification, and failure handling.

Fix correctly: Provide a reversible migration or a forward-compatible recovery plan with verification.

Constraints: Make schema changes rolling-deploy safe (OPS-015). Add data-correctness tests (TST-015).

Acceptance: Migrations have a recovery path. Add a test verifying migration and its rollback/forward-fix.

checks.question: Do code changes require simultaneous deploy of all services, clients, workers, or schema (deployment not backward/forward compatible)? (OPS-014)

onYes.title: Fix incompatible deployment (OPS-014): support rolling deploys
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Requiring a lockstep deploy causes downtime and risky big-bang releases.

Find all instances: Search for changes that assume all components deploy at once (incompatible wire/schema/contract changes).

Fix correctly: Make changes backward/forward compatible so components can deploy independently (additive changes, tolerate old+new).

Constraints: Version contracts (API-001). Use expand/contract for schema (OPS-015).

Acceptance: Components deploy independently. Add a compatibility test across old/new versions.

checks.question: Do migrations rename/drop/change fields before all old code paths stop using them (schema change unsafe for rolling deploy)? (OPS-015)

onYes.title: Fix unsafe schema change (OPS-015): use expand/migrate/contract
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Destructive schema changes during a rolling deploy break old instances still running.

Find all instances: Search migrations for rename/drop/type-change of fields still used by deployed code.

Fix correctly: Use expand/migrate/contract across separate deploys: add new, migrate/dual-write, switch reads, then remove old once no code uses it.

Constraints: Coordinate with deploy compatibility (OPS-014).

Acceptance: Schema changes are rolling-deploy safe. Document/sequence the expand-contract steps and add migration tests.

checks.question: Are admin, billing, security, access-control, data-export, or destructive actions performed without audit records (missing audit trail for privileged action)? (OPS-016)

onYes.title: Fix missing audit trail (OPS-016): record privileged actions
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Without audit records, privileged/destructive actions can't be investigated or attributed.

Find all instances: Search admin/billing/security/access-control/export/destructive actions for audit logging.

Fix correctly: Record actor, action, target, time, source, and outcome for privileged actions in a tamper-evident audit log.

Constraints: Don't log secrets/PII beyond what's needed (CSP-017). Make audit logs durable.

Acceptance: Privileged actions are audited. Add a test asserting an audit record is written for a privileged action.

checks.question: Are user-controlled or high-cardinality values used as metric labels, log event names, or trace attributes (unbounded log/metric cardinality)? (OPS-017)

onYes.title: Fix unbounded cardinality (OPS-017): use bounded labels
onYes.prompt:
Problem: High-cardinality labels (user IDs, URLs) explode metric/trace storage and cost.

Find all instances: Search metric labels/log event names/trace attributes for user-controlled or high-cardinality values.

Fix correctly: Use bounded label sets; move high-cardinality identifiers into sampled logs/traces, not metric dimensions.

Constraints: Keep correlation possible via IDs in logs (OPS-003).

Acceptance: Metric/label cardinality is bounded. Add a check asserting no unbounded values are used as labels.

checks.question: Are secrets, PII, tokens, URLs with credentials, or user content present in metrics, tags, or traces (sensitive value in metric/tag/trace)? (OPS-018)

onYes.title: Fix sensitive telemetry (OPS-018): redact or omit sensitive values
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Sensitive values in telemetry leak to observability backends and dashboards.

Find all instances: Search metrics/tags/traces for secrets, PII, tokens, credentialed URLs, or user content.

Fix correctly: Redact or omit sensitive telemetry before emission.

Constraints: Coordinate with log/response redaction (CSP-002/CSP-017).

Acceptance: No sensitive value reaches telemetry. Add a test asserting a sensitive value is redacted/omitted from emitted telemetry.

checks.question: Do severe logs/errors lack an actionable message, category, dependency name, or runbook hint (critical error lacks operator action)? (OPS-019)

onYes.title: Fix non-actionable critical errors (OPS-019): add operator guidance
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Critical errors without actionable context slow incident response.

Find all instances: Search severe logs/errors for missing actionable message, category, dependency name, or runbook hint.

Fix correctly: Include safe context and operator action guidance (what failed, which dependency, suggested next step) without leaking secrets.

Constraints: Don't leak sensitive details (ERR-014/CSP-002).

Acceptance: Critical errors are actionable. Review/update the affected error messages.

checks.question: Is behavior depending on environment, config, region, cloud, filesystem, OS, or deployment mode left untested (environment-specific behavior untested)? (OPS-020)

onYes.title: Fix untested environment behavior (OPS-020): add environment-matrix tests
onYes.prompt:
Problem: Environment-dependent behavior that's untested breaks in some deployments.

Find all instances: Search for behavior branching on environment/config/region/cloud/filesystem/OS/deployment mode without tests.

Fix correctly: Add environment-matrix tests or startup config validation covering the relevant variations.

Constraints: Don't rely on a single environment. Validate config at startup (OPS-009).

Acceptance: Environment-specific behavior is tested/validated. Add tests for the key environment variations.
